precepts.text: Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah. There is the proof of where our people fled.
precepts.point: And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness. The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
Isaiah tells Moab, “hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth”, and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler.” The outcast is us, the Israelites; that is why verse 1 speaks of “the mount of the daughter of Zion.” During the time of Nebuchadnezzar many Israelites fled and hid amongst Moab, and the spoiler they hid from was Nebuchadnezzar.

Jeremiah is the proof of where our people fled: “Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.”

Where were they? In Moab, among the Ammonites, and in Edom. When the king of Babylon came through, Judah scattered into those lands and hid there, just as Isaiah told Moab to hide them. And “Sela” in verse 1 is Petra, which is Edom; they call Edom Petra today.

There is a dual meaning behind these scriptures. What happened with our people and Moab in the time of Nebuchadnezzar speaks again to the last days, when Moab is China and our people are outcasts among the nations, until “the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land” and the throne of Christ is established.

precepts.text: Even the heathen knew Israel prospered while keeping the law and was led captive once they departed from it.
precepts.point: The nations always knew why we went into captivity; it is sin, the breaking of the Most High's laws, that becomes our weakness and how we are overcome.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

precepts.why:
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, a heathen, told Jeremiah that the Lord had pronounced this evil because “ye have sinned against the Lord, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you.” The nations always knew why we went into captivity. Judith records the heathen saying the same: “And whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them.”

“But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their’s, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground, and their cities were taken by the enemies.” Even the heathen knew Israel prospered while keeping the law and was led captive once they departed from it. It is sin, the breaking of the Most High's laws, that becomes our weakness and how we are overcome.

points: The word came to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let him go from Ramah, where he had been bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah being carried away to Babylon; Jeremiah was let go when Jerusalem was seized.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: The captain, a heathen, told Jeremiah that the Most High had pronounced this evil upon the place because the people sinned against Him and would not obey His voice, so this thing had come upon them.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: The captain loosed Jeremiah from the chains on his hands and gave him an ultimatum, either to come with him to Babylon where he would be looked after well, or to remain in the land as he pleased.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: He directed Jeremiah to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the cities of Judah, gave him food and a reward, and let him go; Gedaliah was one of Jeremiah's good friends.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people left in the land.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: When all the captains of the forces in the fields heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor and had committed to him the men, women, children, and the poor of the land who were not carried away, they came together to him at Mizpah.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Gedaliah swore to them not to fear serving the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them; the war was over and they were already conquered.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: All the Jews scattered in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and the other countries heard of the remnant left under Gedaliah and returned to the land of Judah, gathering wine and summer fruits in abundance.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Johanan the son of Kareah and the captains of the forces came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him that Baalis the king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay him, but Gedaliah believed them not.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah, offering to kill Ishmael himself so that Gedaliah would not be slain and the gathered remnant scattered.
Gedaliah forbade Johanan to do it, saying he spoke falsely of Ishmael, and refused to believe the plot.
